role: ArchiveStore's persistence mechanics: the locked write path (_archive with tombstone/schema gates, rrSeries splice, same-night merge, atomic write + index save with rollback), the hash-checked read path, dual-format (encrypted/legacy) decoding, split-night segment normalisation, tombstones + deletion times, and the import-duplicate check (sessionExists). Batch archiving is in Archive+Batch.swift.
types: ArchiveStore: extension — internal write/read/delete/batch mechanics over SessionArchive state
ArchiveStore.StoredRRSeries: enum — preserved(beats, viaRawDecode)/noBeatsStored/unreadable outcome of reading stored beats
ArchiveStore.OverlapVerdict: enum (private) — keepLonger/distinct for segment dedupe
ArchiveStore.PriorFile: struct — a file's bytes, existence and pending-encryption state before a write, for rollBackWrite
state: static ArchiveStore.minMeaningfulSegment = 600 s (segments shorter are dropped as artifacts)
ud:archive.deletionTimes (standard suite; [uuidString: epoch seconds] dictionary, ArchiveStore.deletionTimesKey)
mem:ArchiveStore.unsavedDeletionTimes (static OSAllocatedUnfairLock<[UUID: UnsavedDeletionTime]>: deletion-time changes staged but not yet in UserDefaults)
file:<archiveDirectory>/<uuid>.json (session files written by writeAndIndex; writeBatchSession in Archive+Batch.swift writes the same files)
toplevel: Imports os (OSAllocatedUnfairLock). File-scope private func verifyHash (fileprivate). No global state besides the static constants, the deletion-times queue/key and the staged deletion-time overlay above. Header comment states underscored/private helpers assume the caller holds archive.archiveLock while exists/delete/entries etc. and archiveBatch (Archive+Batch.swift) take it themselves.

units.does: Locked-caller write entry: runs guardWritable (tombstone + newer-schema gates), splices stored rrSeries onto a beat-less incoming session (throws, writing nothing, when the stored file cannot be read or decrypted now), then either folds an overnight into a same-night/copy target (sameNightMerge) or writes file + index (writeAndIndex); returns the resulting index entry.

branches.cond: sameNightMerge returned an entry (session was folded into an existing archived session)
branches.effect: return that entry (keyed by the OLDER session's id); otherwise fall through to writeAndIndex

units.does: Throws sessionWasDeleted when the session id is tombstoned, or newerSchemaVersion(v) when the session was decoded from a schema newer than HRVSession.currentSchemaVersion; otherwise returns.

branches.effect: log + throw ArchiveError.sessionWasDeleted (blocks CloudKit-race resurrection); else continue
log warning + throw newerSchemaVersion(v); else return normally (nil version = legacy, allowed)

units.does: If the incoming session has rrSeries == nil and the id is already indexed, reads the stored copy's beats (storedRRSeries) and splices them back onto the session before it is written; returns the (possibly patched) session. When neither reader can open the stored file, throws the read/decrypt error (storedBytesError) so a transient failure never overwrites intact beats; only bytes that read and decrypt but do not decode let the write go ahead without beats.

branches.cond: session.rrSeries == nil AND archive.index contains this id
branches.effect: continue to splice; otherwise return session unchanged (has beats or is new)
break silently; when true log a warning that the raw reader salvaged the beats and the re-archive heals the hash
nothing to splice (file read fine, no beats)

branches.cond: case .unreadable and the stored bytes cannot be read or decrypted now
branches.effect: log .error and throw that error; the write is abandoned

branches.cond: case .unreadable otherwise (bytes read and decrypt but do not decode)
branches.effect: log .error and return the session WITHOUT beats, so the following write replaces the corrupt file

units.does: The error from reading the indexed file's bytes and turning them into plaintext (plaintextBytes decrypts encrypted files), or nil when that succeeds, the id is not indexed, or there is no file.

branches.cond: no file at the resolved path

units.does: Reads the stored session for id: via hash-checked _retrieve first; on failure via the hash-agnostic loadAndDecodeSessionFile on the indexed file. Returns preserved(beats, viaRawDecode), noBeatsStored, or unreadable.

branches.effect: return .preserved(rrSeries, viaRawDecode:false) or .noBeatsStored when its rrSeries is nil; errors are discarded by try? and fall to the raw path

branches.cond: an index entry exists AND the raw decode succeeded
branches.effect: continue; otherwise (no entry, or decode/decrypt threw — error discarded) return .unreadable

units.does: For a NEW overnight (not a re-archive, merge not skipped, no explicit linkedSessionIds) with a same-sleep gap configured, finds a merge target; if found, loads it, merges the incoming session's data into it (SessionMerger) and re-archives the existing session, discarding the new UUID. Returns the merged entry, or nil to write standalone; a target that cannot be loaded (retrieve throws, or the id lookup misses) or re-archived throws instead.

branches.effect: hasExplicitLinks true → guard fails → return nil

branches.cond: not a re-archive, not skipped, sessionType == .overnight, no explicit links, sameSleepGap non-nil (merge mode not .off), mergeTarget found
branches.effect: proceed to merge; any failing condition returns nil (caller writes standalone)

branches.cond: existing.recoveryScore nil / session.recoveryScore nil (?? "nil" in log)

branches.effect: throw ArchiveError.fileNotFound (caught below, rethrown); never a standalone write

branches.cond: catch: _retrieve, the lookup miss or the recursive _archive threw
branches.effect: log warning and rethrow so the caller does not mark the backup archived

flags.text: The doc says a NEW overnight that is a copy of an archived recording merges into it, but the guard requires sameSleepGap(for:) to be non-nil, which is nil when sessionMergeMode == .off; with merging off an overlapping copy with a different UUID is written standalone by _archive, while archiveBatch (archiveOne) merges the same copy because it calls mergeTarget with a nil gap. MergeTarget's own comment says with merging off 'only copies of the same recording merge'.

units.does: Encodes the session (encrypted when possible), snapshots the file it replaces (PriorFile: bytes, existence, pending-encryption state; throws if the bytes cannot be read), writes <uuid>.json through writeArchiveBytes (protection by format; ledger restored if the write throws), replaces/appends its index entry and saves the index; on save failure rollBackWrite restores the previous index, file, protection class and ledger entry, then rethrows.

branches.cond: a file already existed and cannot be read
branches.effect: PriorFile throws → whole write aborted before anything is written
rollBackWrite (index, caches, previous file with its protection class and ledger entry, or removal of the new file) then rethrow; on success return the new entry

units.does: Records whether a file exists at url, its bytes when it does (throws if they cannot be read), and whether the session id is queued in PendingEncryptionLedger (its bytes plaintext awaiting re-encryption).

branches.effect: read its bytes (throws); else data nil

units.does: Encodes the session with SessionArchive.sessionEncoder (compact sortedKeys) via SessionFileCodec.encodeForDisk and returns (bytes, sha256 of bytes-as-written, the disk format). No ledger change: the write (writeArchiveBytes) handles that.

Restores the pre-write state after a failed index save: puts the index back, drops the derived caches, and either rewrites the previous bytes through writeArchiveBytes with the format they had (plaintext pending encryption → .completeFileProtection and re-queued; otherwise encrypted protection and ledger cleared) or, when there was no file before, clears the ledger entry and removes the new file. File failures are logged (attempt), not thrown. Caller holds the lock (writeAndIndex, ArchiveMigrations.relinkUnderLock).

branches.effect: clear ledger entry, remove the new file

units.does: Locked-caller hash-checked read: looks up the entry, reads bytes, verifies SHA256 against entry.fileHash, decrypts/passes through to plaintext, and decodes HRVSession with the full sessionDecoder (rrSeries included). Returns nil when the id is not indexed.
Resolves the entry's file URL (relative or legacy absolute) and returns its bytes; throws fileNotFound if absent, rethrows read errors (e.g. EPERM).

Turns stored bytes into plaintext JSON: 'FR'-prefixed bytes are decrypted (errors rethrown); JSON-looking bytes pass through; anything else is decrypt-attempted with failure falling back to the raw bytes.

branches.cond: catch: decrypt of FR bytes threw
decrypt of non-JSON, non-FR bytes fails (?? fallback)
branches.effect: return the raw bytes (decoder then reports dataCorrupted); success returns decrypted legacy Format 2/3 plaintext

units.does: True when data has >=2 bytes starting 0x46 0x52 ('FR' magic of current EncryptionManager format).
Scans up to the first 8 bytes skipping whitespace/BOM-first-byte; true if the first significant byte is '{' or '['; false otherwise or if only whitespace in the first 8 bytes.

branches.cond: for each of the first 8 bytes
branches.effect: iterate; falling off the end returns false

units.does: Reads a session file at a URL and decodes it with the given decoder, handling FR-encrypted (decrypt, errors thrown), plaintext JSON, and legacy Format 2/3 ciphertext (decrypt attempted, failure falls back to raw bytes). No hash check.

branches.effect: swallow; decode raw bytes so JSONDecoder throws dataCorrupted

units.does: For a session with linkedSessionIds, loads each linked session's span, normalises all segments (own + linked) for split-night display, and returns only the linked ones (excluding the current id), or nil when there are none.

branches.effect: current end = startDate → normalizer returns [] (end not after start) → result nil

units.does: Loads one linked session via archive.retrieve (full, hash-checked, takes lock) and returns its (id,start,end) segment; nil when missing, zero/negative length, or the read throws (logged).

branches.effect: end = start → next guard returns nil
return nil; else return the segment
log warning and return nil (segment silently missing from display)

units.does: Pure: computes the current session's own stretch, merges it with linked segments, drops segments <10 min, sorts by start, collapses duplicate/contained ranges and merges ranges separated by < SleepConstants.defaultSplitGapMinutes.

Pure: derives the current session's unique segment — after the latest linked end (child case), before the earliest linked start (parent case), or its own bounds — and returns nil when shorter than 10 minutes.

branches.cond: max linked end exists and lies strictly inside (start, end)
else min linked start exists and is after start

units.does: Pure: walks start-sorted segments, keeping the longer of any pair judged the same segment (overlapVerdict) and appending distinct ones.
Replaces the last kept segment with the candidate when the candidate is strictly longer.

branches.effect: return without change; else replace last

units.does: Pure: .keepLonger when starts and ends are both within 5 min, when the pair overlaps >= duplicateContainmentRatio (0.85) of the shorter, or when either is contained in the other within 5 min tolerance; else .distinct.

branches.cond: either range contained in the other (±5 min)

units.does: Pure: true when the overlap of two segments is >= 0.85 of the shorter one's duration.
Pure: segment end minus start in seconds.
Pure: merges consecutive segments whose gap is shorter than SleepConstants.defaultSplitGapMinutes*60, extending the earlier segment's end (keeps the earlier id).

branches.cond: gap from last end >= continuity threshold
branches.effect: append as a separate segment; else extend last.end to max(last.end, segment.end)

units.does: O(1) id→entry lookup using the cached sessionIdLookup dictionary, building and caching it from archive.index (last duplicate wins) on a cache miss. Caller holds the lock.

branches.effect: return lookup[id]; else build, store and return

units.does: Takes the lock and returns all index entries sorted newest-first by date, using/filling sortedEntriesCache.

branches.effect: return it; else sort, cache and return

units.does: Returns sorted entries filtered by tag ids: excluded if any exclude-tag matches; included if includeTags empty or any include-tag matches.

branches.cond: exclude set non-empty and intersects the entry's tags

branches.effect: keep entry; else keep only when it intersects

flags.text: Only reached through SessionArchive.entries(includingTags:) whose only caller is EmuquTests/ArchiveIntegrityTests.swift:270; no production code filters by tags here.

units.does: Returns sorted entries whose start date lies within [startDate, endDate] inclusive.
Takes the lock and reports whether archive.index holds the id.
Takes the lock and reports whether any entry's start date lies within ±toleranceMinutes (default 30) of the date.

Takes the lock; for an indexed id logs a breadcrumb, removes it from the index with a tombstone + deletion time (dropFromIndex, throws on save failure), then moves its file to Trash/ (falls back to deleting it). Unknown ids are a silent no-op.

flags.text: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md says delete() '(1) adds to deletedSessionIds and persists, (2) removes from active index, (3) deletes file'; the code moves the file to Trash/<uuid>.session (kept until expireTrash, 90 days) and only deletes it when the move fails.

units.does: Removes the entry from index, inserts a tombstone, records a deletion time, then saves deleted.json then index.json; on any save failure re-appends the entry, removes the tombstone and deletion time, nils caches, re-saves deleted.json (attempt) and rethrows.

branches.effect: roll back in-memory index/tombstone/deletion time, rewrite deleted.json without the id (error swallowed by attempt), rethrow

units.does: Takes the lock; true when the id is in deletedSessionIds.
Takes the lock and returns a copy of deletedSessionIds.

Takes the lock; removes the tombstone, forgets the deletion time and saves deleted.json (throws). Used for trash restore, cross-device restore adoption, and (through SessionArchive.forgetDeletedSession) forgetting a dismissed lost session.
Takes the lock; inserts a tombstone for the id (need not be archived), records its deletion time and saves deleted.json (throws).

This device's recorded deletion time for the id: a change staged on deletionTimesQueue but not yet written wins (recorded → its time, forgotten → nil), else the UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes value (epoch seconds → Date), nil when none. A deletion recorded a moment ago is therefore seen at once.
Returns every UUID that has a recorded deletion time; used to rebuild the tombstone set when deleted.json is unreadable.
Stages now as the id's deletion time (stageDeletionTime): visible to deletionTime(of:) immediately, written to UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes on the serial queue, outside archiveLock.
Stages the removal of the id's deletion time (stageDeletionTime): deletionTime(of:) reads nil at once; the UserDefaults entry is removed on the serial queue.
Records the change in the unsavedDeletionTimes overlay under its lock, then queues persistDeletionTime on deletionTimesQueue.

On deletionTimesQueue: applies the change to the UserDefaults archive.deletionTimes dictionary (set the epoch time or remove the id; an absent dictionary starts empty) and writes it back, then drops the overlay entry unless a newer change for the id was staged meanwhile.
units.entry: Runs on ArchiveStore.deletionTimesQueue, queued by stageDeletionTime.

branches.cond: overlay still holds this same change
branches.effect: remove it; a newer change stays

units.does: Takes the lock; true when any entry's start date is within SessionArchive.Tuning.importDuplicateWindow (3600 s, exclusive) of the date. Import-time duplicate check.
File-private: SHA256-hex of the raw stored bytes compared to entry.fileHash; logs details and throws hashMismatch on mismatch.

branches.effect: return; else log expected/actual/size and throw ArchiveError.hashMismatch
